play: PROMOTE abs_veto_55s into the live paper tournament. It is the #1 shadow variant: a thrust gate + a 55s absorption veto that skips the thrusts that get eaten. The veto is the whole edge — same win/loss sizes as plain thrust, but it doubles the hit-rate by ditching the fakeouts.
rationale: Robustness battery PASSED: +$1,448 over 103 trades, 50% win, ~2:1 reward:risk, worst loss only -$71, max drawdown -$222. Profitable in BOTH chop (+$694) and trend (+$754), 2nd-half BETTER than 1st (no decay), beats the un-vetoed thrust by +$1,040 with HALF the drawdown. Caveat: ~9-day sample; the forward shadow run is green (+$218 today) but wants a red-trend day to fully confirm.

play: RELEGATE rgv_short from the live tournament. Its only edge is one narrow ER band (0.30-0.40); everywhere else it bleeds, and it is the desk's clearest relegation candidate.
rationale: Single-band edge, fragile. It did have one good chop day (+$310 on 07-23), so it is not worthless — but as a standing live gate it does not carry its weight. Free the slot for abs_veto_55s.

play: KEEP the two long-faders (rgv_long, capitulation_long) in the lineup — do NOT relegate. Let the live direction-router be their guard: it benches them automatically in a proven down-trend, which is the only thing that hurt them.
rationale: The gates are not broken, they were direction-blind: their ER bands read cleanliness not direction, so they faded a clean down-trend (rgv_long -$361 in an hour on 07-23). The router fixes exactly that, and on a chop day rgv_long was the desk's best gate (+$92.5). Keep + guard beats relegate.

play: The 15-min-timer direction-router works (+$580 Mon-Thu backtest, live-validated) but has a reaction lag and whipsaw cost. Interrogate whether a more elegant mechanism (per-gate direction-guard in-code / event-driven / continuous in-tournament gating) does the job better.
rationale: Keep the router live as-is for now; the report researches + backtests the alternatives. The likely end-state is an in-code per-gate guard (per-tick, no polling lag, no switch-file), with the router as the automated bridge. Not a this-week change.

play: DO NOT ARM any new run-catching entry. Every causal entry I invented (flow-continuation, volume-breakout, chase-the-flow, vacuum-fade, Donchian breakout) is a 48-52% coin-flip that bleeds after realistic cost.
rationale: The runs ARE real money (+$4,388 with perfect hindsight timing) and the exit is fine — the problem is purely the entry: a real-time run-start is statistically indistinguishable from the chop-bursts around it. Family B (vacuum snap-backs, ~half the pot) is confirmed structurally unpredictable. Durable negative lesson, no green light.

topic: Donchian as a DETECTOR (not a gate)
play: SHADOW the 5-min Donchian breakout as a non-trading 'a run may be starting' LABEL only — feeding the regime/shadow router, never as a capital gate.
rationale: A lousy entry (bleeds -$5,056 traded) but a great detector — it flags 48 of 49 runs in real time. Zero capital, zero P&L claim; it may earn its keep as a signal the router listens to, not a trade.

play: INVESTIGATE next Friday: does the far-side order book (58.9M depth rows) thin out BEFORE a run in a way price/volume/flow can't see? The one stone left unturned.
rationale: Price, volume and aggressor flow all failed to separate run-starts from chop. The order book is the only microstructure signal not yet tested against the runs. Next week's greenfield subject.
